Hon'ble Smt. Justice Rajani Dubey, J  Hon'ble Shri Justice Sanjay Kumar Jaiswal, J  Order on Board

Per Rajani Dubey, J Challenge in this appeal is to the legality and validity of the judgment and decree dated 30.10.2021 passed by Family Court, Surajpur in Civil Suit No.37A/2019 whereby suit filed under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act by the appellant seeking decree of divorce has been dismissed.

02. The appellant/plaintiff filed a suit under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act with the averments that marriage between the appellant and the respondent was solemnized on 19.5.2001 as per Hindu rites and rituals and from their wedlock two children were born.
After marriage, they were living in a joint family.

However, the behaviour of the respondent towards the appellant has Ravindra Kumar Soni vs Smt. Pramila Soni on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78911106/
1 been cruel since beginning.

sentences.text: She used to quarrel with his father and brother unnecessarily and pressurize the appellant for living separately.
Being fed up with her conduct, the appellant's father allowed them to live separately in his house situated at Namadgiri.
As the appellant's betel shop was removed by the Municipal Corporation, he was in financial crisis.
When the respondent was running a beauty parlour from home, she came in contact with one lady with whom she used to roam around, which was objected by the appellant but she paid no heed to it.
She used to taunt the appellant saying that she is earning more than him from her beauty parlour and decline to discharge her marital obligations.
In August, 2015 she along with the children and her articles went to her maternal home and lodged a report against the appellant regarding demand of dowry.

Though in the year 2016 the appellant filed an application under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act for restitution of conjugal rights and tried his level best to keep her with him but it was dismissed on the assurance of the respondent to live with him.
However, the respondent came to her matrimonial home and went back with her remaining articles to her maternal home.
They are living separately since March, 2015 and no physical relation was established between them since then.
Though the appellant expressed his willingness before the Parivar Paramarsh Kendra for keeping the respondent with him but she did not turn up there.
03. The respondent/defendant being absent was proceeded ex- parte.
Even no written statement was filed by her.
04. Learned Family Court after hearing the appellant/plaintiff, considering his pleadings and the documents on record, dismissed the suit by the impugned judgment and decree.
Hence this appeal.
05. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the learned Family Court has committed a gross illegality and irregularity in dismissing the appellant's suit.

It has failed to properly appreciate the evidence adduced by the appellant and without application of mind dismissed the suit holding that no cruelty has been caused by the respondent to the appellant.
No issues or settlement of dispute has been pointed out in respect of the allegation of frivolous criminal cases lodged by the respondent.
Learned Family Court ought to have appreciated the fact that it is the respondent who herself left the matrimonial home and is living separately.

The application for maintenance filed by her was dismissed by order dated 23.11.2019 and the complaint case filed by her was also dismissed by order dated 29.3.2019 due to her non-appearance before the Court.
Looking to the conduct of the respondent and the pleadings of the appellant supported by the documentary evidence, the learned Family Court was not justified in dismissing the suit of the appellant.
Therefore, the impugned judgment and decree are liable to be set aside.

06. In this appeal, the appellant has also filed an application under Order 41 Rule 27 read with Section 151 of CPC and prayed for taking on record the charge sheet (Annexure A/2) filed on the report of respondent/wife against one person for the offence under Section 366(2)(n) of IPC which shows that she has been living in adultery.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant was not able to file these documents before the learned Family Court as the same were not handy with him during the proceedings and after great difficulty, these documents could be traced by him.
Contents of the documents itself show that matrimonial life of the appellant has been devastated by the respondent and she was enjoying her life with another person.

2 aforesaid documents being relevant may be taken on record for proper adjudication of the matter in the interest of justice.

sentences.text: 07. On the other hand, supporting the impugned judgment and decree, learned counsel for the respondent contends that the learned Family Court upon proper appreciation of the oral and documentary evidence on record right came to the conclusion that no cruelty or desertion has been committed by the respondent against the appellant and dismissed the suit.
This appeal is without any substance and as such, liable to be dismissed.

As regards the application (IA No.01/2022),
learned counsel for the respondent strongly opposed the prayer of the appellant and submits that if these documents are taken on record at this stage, the respondent is also entitled to be afforded an opportunity to file document and additional evidence in rebuttal.

08. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.
09.

It is clear from the record of the learned Family Court that the appellant/husband filed an application under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act against the respondent/wife on the ground of cruelty and desertion, and after appreciation of oral and documentary evidence, the learned Family Court having found no cruelty and desertion committed by the respondent/wife, dismissed the application of the appellant/husband by the impugned judgment and decree.
10.

Here the appellant has filed an application under Order 41 Rule 27 read with Section 151 of CPC for taking on record the charge sheet filed on the complaint of the appellant's wife against one person for the offence under Section 376(2)(n) of IPC.
A bare perusal of the FIR and the charge sheet would show that the respondent/wife was living in adultery with the accused.

Order 41 Rule 27 of CPC reads as under:
"ORDER XLI APPEALS FROM ORIGINAL DECREES 27. Production of additional evidence in Appellate Court.-

( 1) The parties to an appeal shall not be entitled to produce additional evidence,
whether oral or documentary, in the Appellate Court.

But if - (a) the Court from whose decree the appeal is preferred has refused to admit evidence which ought to have been admitted, or 1[(aa) the party seeking to produce additional evidence, establishes that notwithstanding the exercise of due diligence, such evidence was not within his knowledge or could not, after the exercise of due diligence, be produced by him at the time when the decree appealed against was passed, or]
(b) the Appellate Court requires any document to be produced or any witness to be examined to enable it to pronounce judgment, or for any other substantial cause, the Appellate Court may allow such evidence or document to be produced, or witness to be examined.

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Union of India Vs. K.V. Lakshman and others,
(2016) 13 SCC 124 held in para 36 of its judgment as under:
"36. Order 41 Rule 27 of the Code is a provision which enables the party to file additional evidence at the first and second appellate stage.

entities.text:
Union of India Vs. K.V. Lakshman and others,
(2016) 13 SCC 124
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If the party to appeal is able to satisfy the appellate Court that there is justifiable reason for not filing such evidence at the trial stage and that the additional evidence is relevant and material for deciding the rights of the parties which are the subject matter of the lis, the Court should allow the party to file such additional evidence.
After all, the Court has to do substantial justice to the parties.
Merely because the Court allowed one party to file additional evidence in appeal would not by itself mean that the Court has also decided the entire case in his favour and accepted such evidence.
Indeed once the additional evidence is allowed to be taken on record, the appellate Court is under obligation to give opportunity to the other side to file additional evidence by way of rebuttal."
12. From the charge sheet (Annexure A/2) it is clear that the complainant in the said criminal case is wife of the appellant.
In the FIR she stated to have been living with the accused after being deserted by her husband.
The appellant has filed an affidavit in support of this application whereas no counter affidavit has been filed by the respondent.

13. In view of above, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the issue involved in the case and the nature and relevance of the documents sought to be taken on record, the application (IA No.01 of 2022) under Order 41 Rule 27 read with Section 151 of CPC deserves to be and is,
accordingly, allowed.
Consequently, the aforesaid documents (Annexure A/2) are taken on record.
14. In the result, the impugned judgment and decree dated 30.10.2021 are hereby set aside.

The matter is remitted to the learned Family Court, Surajpur for deciding the application under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 filed by the appellant/husband afresh after permitting both the parties to adduce additional evidence, oral and documentary, amend their pleadings if they so desire, and affording them opportunity of hearing, on its own merits in accordance with law.
Parties to appear before the concerned Family Court on 07-11-2024.
The appeal is thus allowed to the above extent.
It is made clear that nothing in this order shall be construed as an expression of opinion on merits of the case and the learned Family Court to decide the matter on its own merits.
